newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee oversold but may add to losses.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee oversold but may add to losses.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures are in slightly oversold territory, but still have room to dip further in the near term, analysts said on Wednesday.
July coffee was calculated to open down $20 but some traders expected an opening nearer $10 lower.
July closed $14 lower at $1,655 on Tuesday, mirroring profit-taking losses in New York after CSCE May jumped to contract highs on Monday.

"In the near term, (July) is oversold, but it could still go a bit lower," said independent technical analyst Elli Gifford. Initial support rested at Tuesday's close of $1,655 with more support slightly below at $1,650.
But Gifford did not expect those supports to hold for long. She expected a test of stronger support at $1,625 in the near term. "That will probably hold," she said.
Gifford mostly attributed her slightly lower outlook for July coffee to strong resistance at $1,700, the March 18 high.

July pierced the $1,700 barrier on Monday when the contract traded as high as $1,705. But its failure to hold and add to those gains to fill a chart gap left from the March 12 low of $1,730 and Monday's high had tempered the market's bullishness in the near term.

A slightly cooler attitude in the near term toward London's robusta market also came after New York's July coffee contract traded an inside day on Tuesday, some analysts said. CSCE July traded between 193.00 and 188.00 on Tuesday versus the previous day's range of 199.00 and 187.50.
